intro_html: Seared pork chops smothered in a creamy mushroom gravy over mashed potatoes. Steakhouse comfort at 40 grams of protein and 591 calories per plate, for about $2.46. The gravy is built on the browned bits the chops leave behind, which is flavor you already paid for.
cost_closing_html: About $2.46 a bowl for smothered pork chops with mashed potatoes. A smothered chop plate runs $14 to $17 at a steakhouse or diner, and it comes with exactly zero leftovers.
shop_smart: Pork chops are the whole budget here at $21.88 for 5.25 pounds. This is a recipe worth timing to the weekly ad; sale chops can cut the batch cost by a fifth.
Four packs of white mushrooms for $4.76 make the gravy taste far more expensive than it is. Mushrooms are the cheapest way to make cream sauce eat like a steakhouse.
Whole potatoes for the mash cost $1.36. That is about 10 cents of side dish per plate.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Start the potatoes: peel, chunk, and boil in salted water 15 to 20 minutes until fork tender. Drain and mash with a spoonful of the butter and a pinch of salt. Cover and keep warm.

Season the chops with salt and pepper and dust lightly with some of the flour. Sear in olive oil in your big skillet, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and the centers read 145 F. Rest on a plate.
Melt the butter in the same skillet and cook the sliced mushrooms without crowding until browned, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the remaining flour and stir 1 to 2 minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits, then stir in the heavy cream. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Return the chops and any juices to the gravy for a minute to warm through.
Portion mashed potatoes into 14 containers, top with a chop, and ladle mushroom gravy over each.
portion_html: Weigh the pot of mashed potatoes, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14 for the base, then split the chops and gravy evenly on top. Each plate lands at about 591 calories with 40 grams of protein.

steps: Boil and mash the potatoes with butter and salt.
Season and flour-dust the chops, then sear to 145 F and rest.
Brown mushrooms in butter with garlic, then cook in the flour.
Whisk in broth, Worcestershire, and cream and simmer into a gravy; return the chops.
Portion potatoes, chops, and gravy into 14 containers.
